standard.title: Internal components and function
standard.description: Investigate the main internal components of common digital systems and their function
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore and describe a range of digital systems and their peripherals for a variety of purposes (AC9TDI4K01). They understand that digital systems have input and output components. They have not yet investigated what happens inside a digital system — internal components and their specific functions remain unexplored.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the main internal components of common digital systems (CPU, memory, input/output components, storage) and explain how each component performs a specific function within the system.

nodes.label: Digital systems are made of parts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that digital systems are made up of distinct internal components, each performing a specific function
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least two internal components of a digital system and state what each does
nodes.typical_width: Identify the main internal components (CPU, RAM, storage, input/output) of a familiar digital system such as a tablet or desktop; describe the function of each component in plain language
wider: Compare internal components across different digital systems — a smartphone versus a gaming console versus a laptop — identifying which components are shared and which differ
Investigate the internal components of a telehealth system used to access ultrasound imagery in remote communities, identifying which components support sending and receiving large image files

response_modes.reason: Students at this node commonly confuse 'the device' with 'the component' — treating the whole system as a single thing. Seeing the same component (e.g. a CPU) appear in different devices (tablet, console, laptop) with different physical forms but the same function helps students separate the component from any single device form factor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The telehealth direction is genuinely rich — it situates internal components in a socially meaningful context (remote health access) and makes the function of specific components (large image storage/transmission) concrete and consequential.
success_criteria: Names at least two internal components of a digital system
States the function of each named component in plain language
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify what each component does cannot reason about how components coordinate in N2 — the 'how they work together' task requires knowing each part's role as a prerequisite.

nodes.label: How CPU, memory and I/O work together
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how the CPU, memory and input/output components work together to perform a task
nodes.minimum_width: Trace through a simple calculation or task (e.g. entering numbers and getting a sum) and identify which component handles each step — input, processing, memory, output
nodes.typical_width: Explain how CPU, RAM and input/output components each play a role in completing a simple task; describe what would happen if one component were missing or very slow
wider: Investigate how video conferencing systems combine multiple input/output components (camera, microphone, screen, speaker) and explain how the CPU coordinates them simultaneously
Explore how a calculator app on a tablet uses each component differently from a web browser — which components are used most and why?

response_modes.reason: Students need to reason about a process rather than just name components. The input → process → memory → output chain is a reasoning scaffold, not just a label set. Explicitly tracing a task step-by-step helps students build this as a thinking pattern rather than a memorised sequence.

This node is where the individual component facts from Node 1 become a system understanding. Coordinating all four components in a single task trace is the learning — not any one component in isolation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The video conferencing context (especially telehealth) is rich — it requires students to think about multiple simultaneous I/O streams and how the CPU coordinates them, which is a genuine extension of the basic task trace.
success_criteria: Correctly assigns at least three roles (input, process, memory, output) to the correct component in a given task
Explains what each component contributes without treating them as interchangeable
